transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. As you know from the quarterly review context, we're looking to reduce avoidable cloud spend on the production video-transcoding cluster in us-east-2 without changing ownership or region. The current draft policy proposes a peak allowance of 6 GPU nodes, one shared pool for all customers, 30 days of standard logs, and cross-region archival to us-west-2. Before I can make a final decision and publish, our standing cost-review routine requires reliability, security, support, and FinOps to each confirm their operational constraints. I'd like to go around and hear from each of you on whether this draft works from your area's perspective, or what changes you'd need.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something critical before we go further. While checking the transcoder queue for a separate performance ticket this morning, I confirmed that a contracted customer campaign will require 12 GPU nodes continuously on August 17 and August 18. The campaign booking was finalized in the customer system just minutes ago and hasn't yet been copied into the infrastructure cost-review document. A peak allowance of 6 GPU nodes would not be sufficient for that window.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a constraint on the log retention portion of the draft. During an unrelated access-log audit yesterday, I confirmed that production transcoding access logs must be retained for exactly 90 days in an immutable archive. The draft policy's 30-day standard logs retention would not meet this requirement. I'm still waiting for the security ticket number before formally adding this to the review document, but the 90-day immutable retention requirement is confirmed and non-negotiable.

transcript.text: I need to flag a support constraint on the shared-pool and scale-down portion of the draft. I confirmed with the account team this afternoon that the enterprise customer Orchid has a 15-minute queue-latency SLA and must have 2 dedicated GPU nodes excluded from shared-pool scale-down. The account note was updated after the draft policy circulated and has not yet been reflected in the infrastructure proposal. A single shared pool with aggressive scale-down would put Orchid's SLA at risk unless those 2 dedicated nodes are carved out.

transcript.text: I need to flag a FinOps constraint on the cross-region archival portion of the draft. While reconciling the last cloud invoice, I found that the proposed us-west-2 archive would create a recurring cross-region egress charge of approximately $4,000 per month. The invoice investigation is still open, so I haven't yet amended the cost model, but this charge needs to be factored into the decision before the policy is published.

commitments.detail: Update the cost-review document to reflect the 12-GPU-node peak requirement for August 17-18 contracted campaign before policy is published.
Revise peak GPU node allowance from 6 to 12 to accommodate the confirmed August 17-18 campaign requirement.
Revise log retention from 30 days standard to 90 days immutable archive to meet the confirmed security requirement.
Carve out 2 dedicated GPU nodes for Orchid excluded from shared-pool scale-down to protect the 15-minute queue-latency SLA.
Keep archival in-region (us-east-2) to avoid the approximately $4,000/month cross-region egress charge to us-west-2; Theo to amend the cost model accordingly once invoice reconciliation is complete.
Nia to add the security ticket number to the review document once received, confirming the 90-day immutable retention requirement.
